text:
# 什么是其他人还会问（People Also Ask，PAA）？

- 原标题：What Is People Also Ask (PAA)?
- 作者：Flavio Amiel Roborank 创始人
- 原文更新日期：2026-07-15
- 原文：https://roborank.io/glossary/people-also-ask/
- 栏目：[AI Search & GEO](https://roborank.io/ai-search/)
- 说明：中文全文翻译，后附英文原文。原文中的数据、观点、平台说明及推广内容均按原文保留，未经独立验证。

---

## 中文全文

“其他人还会问”（People Also Ask，PAA）是 Google 搜索的一项交互功能，会在靠前的搜索结果附近展示一组相关问题。展开任意问题，就会看到从网页中提取的简短回答及原网页链接；随着搜索者继续点击，Google 还会生成更多相关问题。

### 核心要点

- Google 自己的文档将这项功能称为“相关问题组”；“People Also Ask”则是搜索者熟悉的名称。
- 展开的每个 PAA 问题都会显示一个精选摘要，也就是从高质量网页中引用的答案，并附上来源链接。
- 这项功能是动态的：点击一个问题，Google 就会追加更多相关问题，因此列表可以随着用户的点击不断增长。
- Google 表示，你无法控制 PAA 中显示什么；但它呈现的问题揭示了真实搜索意图，值得围绕这些问题制作内容。
- 由于每个答案都是精选摘要，能赢得精选摘要的写法——针对一个确切问题，给出清楚、自成一体的回答——也正是获得 PAA 展示位的写法。

### PAA 如何运作

PAA 是 Google 预测下一个问题的方式。搜索者输入查询后，Google 会在结果页放置一组相关问题。Google 自己的[视觉元素库](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/visual-elements-gallery)用一个更直白的名称记录这项功能：*相关问题组*，即“一组与用户最初搜索的内容有关的问题，也称为 People Also Ask”。每个问题默认折叠，直到搜索者点击。

展开问题后，里面会显示一个[精选摘要](https://roborank.io/glossary/featured-snippet/)：这与 Google 放在结果最顶部的引用答案采用相同格式，从某个网页提取回答，并在答案下方附上该网页链接。因此，PAA 不是独立的排名系统，而是把精选摘要机制应用到一组相关查询上，每个查询都有自己的引用来源。对于某个具体问题，哪个页面提供的答案最清楚，Google 就会把它提取到那个位置。

这个模块也是动态的。每当搜索者展开一个问题，Google 就会在列表底部追加更多相关问题，因此只要用户继续点击，问题组就可以继续扩展。这让 PAA 成为观察搜索者好奇心如何分叉的实时窗口，也解释了为什么它与[零点击搜索](https://roborank.io/glossary/zero-click-search/)如此密切相关：搜索者往往可以在结果页内解决一整串问题，而不用访问任何网站。同一套问题图谱，也越来越多地为 [AI Overviews](https://roborank.io/glossary/ai-overviews/) 和生成式搜索在后台运行的[查询扇出](https://roborank.io/glossary/query-fan-out/)提供素材。

关键在于，Google 对你能控制什么有明确界限。它在指南中指出：“虽然你无法控制这里出现什么，但在考虑为网站撰写哪些主题时，关注相关搜索查询可能很有帮助。”你不能强行把一个问题放进这个模块，也不能强行让自己的页面成为答案来源。你只能让自己的答案成为现有材料中最便于提取的那个。

### 什么样的内容会成为 PAA 答案

三个属性决定一个页面能否成为 PAA 答案的来源，这三点都与精选摘要的机制一致：

- **与问题匹配的段落**：标题或句子重述那个确切问题，让 Google 能将查询与文本对应起来。
- **自成一体的答案**：在第一句或前两句直接回答，即使从页面中[提取出来](https://roborank.io/glossary/extractability/)仍然表达正确，因为 Google 展示时不会带上周围的上下文。
- **支撑结构**：简短段落、列表或表格，方便 Google 清晰排版进可展开的面板。

由于每个 PAA 问题都有自己的精选摘要，最有效的写作模式是[答案优先写作](https://roborank.io/glossary/answer-first-writing/)：先给答案，再解释。即使自然搜索排名不错，把答案埋在 300 个词的铺垫后面，也很难赢得这个位置。

### PAA 示例

最清楚、且有文档依据的例子，来自 Google 自己的产品文档，而不是第三方研究，因为其机制说明得格外明确。在[视觉元素库](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/visual-elements-gallery)中，Google 定义了相关问题组，并陈述了影响所有 PAA 策略的两项事实：展开问题会显示精选摘要；网站所有者不能控制其中显示什么。

用一个真实、可重复的查询来理解。搜索一个宽泛的信息型问题，例如“堆肥如何进行”，Google 就会显示相关问题组，其中可能包括“哪些东西不能放进堆肥？”和“堆肥需要多长时间？”展开第一个问题，会出现一个引用自园艺网页的答案框，页面链接就在答案下方，完全符合 Google 文档描述的精选摘要格式。再展开第二个问题，Google 会在列表底部追加新问题，体现文档中提到的动态行为。这些位置都不是网站可以买到或强行占据的；Google 是针对每个问题，选择回答最清晰的那个页面段落。

这一经验直接决定页面应该怎样构建。Google 用精选摘要填充每个 PAA 答案，又明确告诉你无法控制这个模块，因此你唯一能做的，就是提供合适的内容。发布一个页面，在开头用一句清楚、有来源的句子回答其中一个问题，并把格式处理成 Google 能直接提取、不必连带整页其他内容的样子。针对 Google 已经为你的主题展示的问题群都这样做，你就能把一项无法控制的功能，变成可重复获得曝光的来源。这与在主查询上赢得[零位排名](https://roborank.io/glossary/position-zero/)的原则相同。

这也是为什么，即便从未赢得展示位，PAA 问题仍值得收集。Google 免费告诉了你，真实搜索者围绕你的主题会按照什么顺序提问。把这个模块当作研究信息源——一张有依据的意图地图——让它指导你的内容回答哪些问题，并遵循搜索者实际提问的顺序。

### 人们常犯的错误

人们容易把 PAA 当作可以往页面里堆砌的关键词列表，但它实际上是一张问题地图，展示 Google 认为搜索者接下来会问什么。我见过团队抓取一百个 PAA 问题，全部塞进一个臃肿的 FAQ 板块，这几乎从来赢不了展示位。真正获得 PAA 答案位的做法，与赢得精选摘要一样：选定一个问题，在第一句话回答，并确保这句话被拿出页面、没有周围上下文时仍然成立。PAA 不是比数量。每个问题都是一场独立的微型搜索结果竞争，有自己的赢家；Google 会用它找到的最清楚的单一答案填入，而不是选那个把问题重复最多次的页面。

### 常见问题

#### Google 的 People Also Ask 是什么？

这是 Google 搜索的一项功能，会在靠前的结果附近显示一组相关问题。点击问题，会展开一个从网页引用的简短答案及网页链接；每次互动，Google 都会增加更多相关问题。

#### 怎样出现在 People Also Ask 中？

在相关页面靠前的位置，用一句清楚、自成一体的话回答确切问题，再用细节支撑。由于每个 PAA 答案都是精选摘要，赢得精选摘要所需的页面清晰度——直截了当的表述、与问题匹配的标题——也能帮助你获得 PAA 展示位。

#### PAA 和精选摘要是一回事吗？

两者有关联，但并不相同。精选摘要是结果顶部单独的引用答案框；PAA 是一组相关问题，每个问题展开后，都显示自己的精选摘要。PAA 将这种摘要格式扩展到了多个相关查询。

#### 能控制 PAA 中显示什么吗？

不能。Google 明确表示，你无法控制 PAA 中出现什么。你只能针对它展示的问题，发布清楚、来源可靠的答案，间接影响结果。这些问题值得当作一张实时搜索意图地图。

### 要点总结

PAA 将一次搜索转化成不断分叉的追问，每个问题都由某个获得排名页面中的引用段落回答。它奖励的写作能力与任何答案引擎相同：聚焦一个问题，在开头清楚作答，并让答案单独拿出来也能正确理解。模块中的每个问题都是一场独立竞争，能够提供最清晰、最适合直接提取答案的网站会胜出。

## 英文原文

People Also Ask (PAA) is an interactive Google Search feature that displays a cluster of related questions near the top results. Expanding any question reveals a concise answer drawn from a web page, along with a link to that page, and prompts Google to generate further related questions as a searcher keeps clicking.

### Key Takeaways

- Google’s own documentation calls the feature a “related questions group”; “People Also Ask” is the label searchers know it by.
- Each expanded PAA question shows a featured snippet — a quoted answer pulled from a high-quality web page, with a link back to the source.
- The feature is dynamic: interacting with one question makes Google append more related questions, so the list can keep growing as the user clicks.
- Google states you cannot control what appears in PAA, but the questions it surfaces reveal real searcher intent worth building content around.
- Because each answer is a featured snippet, the same writing that wins snippets — a clean, self-contained answer to one exact question — is what earns a PAA slot.

### How People Also Ask Works

People Also Ask is Google’s way of anticipating the next question. After a searcher enters a query, Google places a cluster of related questions on the results page. Google’s own [Visual Elements Gallery](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/visual-elements-gallery) documents the feature under a more literal name: a *related questions group*, “a cluster of questions that are related to what the user initially searched for (also known as ‘People Also Ask’).” Each question sits collapsed until the searcher clicks it.

When a question is expanded, it reveals a [featured snippet](https://roborank.io/glossary/featured-snippet/) — the same quoted-answer format Google uses at the very top of results — drawn from a web page, with a link to that page beneath the answer. So PAA is not a separate ranking system. It is the featured-snippet mechanism replicated across a set of related queries, each with its own quoted source. The page that supplies the cleanest answer to a given question is the one Google lifts into that slot.

The box is also dynamic. Every time a searcher opens a question, Google appends more related questions to the bottom of the list, so the cluster can keep expanding as long as the user keeps clicking. That behavior makes PAA a live window into the branching path of a searcher’s curiosity, which is why it overlaps so heavily with [zero-click search](https://roborank.io/glossary/zero-click-search/): a searcher can often satisfy an entire chain of questions inside the results page without visiting a single site. The same question graph increasingly feeds [AI Overviews](https://roborank.io/glossary/ai-overviews/) and the [query fan-out](https://roborank.io/glossary/query-fan-out/) that generative search runs behind the scenes.

Crucially, Google is explicit about the limits of your control. Its guidance states that “while you can’t control what shows up here, it can be helpful to pay attention to the related search queries when you’re thinking about topics you could write about for your site.” You cannot force a question into the box or force your page into an answer. You can only make your answer the most liftable one available.

### What Feeds a People Also Ask Answer

Three properties decide whether a page becomes the source for a PAA answer, and all three mirror featured-snippet mechanics:

- **A question-matching passage** — a heading or sentence that restates the exact question, so Google can align the query to your text.
- **A self-contained answer** — a direct response in the first sentence or two that reads correctly when [extracted](https://roborank.io/glossary/extractability/) from the page, since Google displays it with no surrounding context.
- **Supporting structure** — a short paragraph, a list, or a table that Google can format cleanly into the expandable panel.

Because each PAA question resolves to its own featured snippet, the writing pattern that wins is [answer-first writing](https://roborank.io/glossary/answer-first-writing/): lead with the answer, then explain. A page that buries its answer under 300 words of preamble rarely wins the slot, even when it ranks well organically.

### Example of People Also Ask

The clearest documented illustration comes from Google’s own product documentation rather than a third-party study, because the mechanics are unusually well specified. In the [Visual Elements Gallery](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/visual-elements-gallery), Google defines the related questions group and states two facts that shape every PAA strategy: expanding a question shows a featured snippet, and site owners cannot control what appears.

Walk through what that means with a real, reproducible query. Search Google for a broad informational question such as “how does composting work,” and a related questions group appears with follow-ups like “What can you not put in compost?” and “How long does compost take?” Expanding the first reveals a boxed answer quoted from a gardening page, with the page’s link directly below it — exactly the featured-snippet format Google’s documentation describes. Open a second question and Google appends new ones to the bottom of the list, demonstrating the dynamic behavior the docs note. None of this is placement a site can buy or force; it is Google selecting, per question, the page whose passage answers it most cleanly.

The lesson generalizes straight to how a page should be built. Because Google fills each PAA answer with a featured snippet, and because it tells you plainly that you cannot control the box, the only lever is supply. You publish a page that answers one of those questions in a single clean, sourced sentence at the top, formatted so Google can lift it without inheriting the rest of your page. Do that across the cluster of questions Google already surfaces for your topic, and you convert an uncontrollable feature into a repeatable source of visibility — the same principle behind winning [position zero](https://roborank.io/glossary/position-zero/) on the head query itself.

That is also why PAA questions are worth harvesting even when you never win a slot. Google is telling you, for free, the exact sequence of questions real searchers ask about your topic. Treat the box as a research feed — a documented map of intent — and let it shape the questions your content answers, in the order a searcher actually asks them.

### The thing people get wrong

The thing people get wrong is treating PAA as a keyword list to stuff, when it is really a map of the questions Google thinks a searcher will ask next. I have watched teams scrape a hundred PAA questions and jam them all into one bloated FAQ block, and it almost never wins the slot. What actually earns a PAA answer is the same discipline that earns a featured snippet: pick one question, answer it in the first sentence, and make that sentence survive being lifted out of the page with no surrounding context. PAA is not a volume game. Each question is a separate micro-SERP with its own winner, and Google fills it with the cleanest single answer it can find, not the page that mentions the question the most times.

### Frequently Asked Questions

#### What is People Also Ask in Google?

It is a Google Search feature that shows a cluster of related questions near the top results. Clicking a question expands a short answer quoted from a web page, plus a link to it, and Google adds more related questions each time you interact.

#### How do you rank in People Also Ask?

Answer the exact question in one clean, self-contained sentence near the top of a relevant page, then support it with detail. Because each PAA answer is a featured snippet, the same on-page clarity that wins snippets — direct phrasing, question-matching headings — is what earns a PAA slot.

#### Is People Also Ask the same as a featured snippet?

They are linked but not identical. A featured snippet is the single quoted answer box at the top of results; People Also Ask is a cluster of related questions, and each one expands to reveal its own featured snippet. PAA multiplies the snippet format across many related queries.

#### Can you control what shows up in People Also Ask?

No. Google states directly that you cannot control what appears in People Also Ask. You can only influence it indirectly by publishing clear, well-sourced answers to the questions it surfaces, which are worth treating as a live map of searcher intent.

### The Bottom Line

People Also Ask turns a single search into a branching set of follow-up questions, each answered by a quoted passage from a ranked page. It rewards the same craft as any answer engine: isolate one question, answer it plainly at the top, and write the answer so it reads correctly on its own. Every question in the box is a separate contest, and the site with the cleanest lift-out answer wins it.
